1. Request callbacks run backwards 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>preprocess_request now runs URL value preprocessors and before_request callbacks from the
>closest child blueprint upward to its parents, rather than app → parent → child. Parent callbacks
>can overwrite child state, and a child callback returning a response can now prevent its parent
>callback from running.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/flask/app.py[1380]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/pull/6216/files#diff-d3e0349504081bb501c611b3954be364188a4cf442056181272e27e830ae446eR1380-R1380) > >```diff >+ names = (None, *req.blueprints) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Request.blueprints delegates to _split_blueprint_path, whose output starts with the fully
>qualified child name and recursively appends parents. The changed tuple therefore feeds both
>callback loops child-first; Flask's previously merged fix explicitly establishes that callbacks
>before the view must run from the app down to the closest nested blueprint.
>
> > [src/flask/wrappers.py[180-195]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/df5c3e8bd120ea314bedeec8cc6165f3d3b7aafc/src/flask/wrappers.py/#L180-L195) > [src/flask/helpers.py[644-651]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/df5c3e8bd120ea314bedeec8cc6165f3d3b7aafc/src/flask/helpers.py/#L644-L651) > [src/flask/app.py[1382-1393]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/df5c3e8bd120ea314bedeec8cc6165f3d3b7aafc/src/flask/app.py/#L1382-L1393) > 🌐 [The merged fix states that before-functions should run from the app down through nested blueprints and fixed this exact callback-order bug.](https://github.com/pallets/flask/pull/4230) > 🌐 [The issue demonstrates that leaf-to-parent execution lets the parent overwrite child state and produce the wrong response.](https://github.com/pallets/flask/issues/4229) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Nested blueprint URL value preprocessors and `before_request` callbacks must execute from the application down through parent blueprints to the closest child. Directly expanding `req.blueprints` reverses that established order because the property is leaf-first. > >## Issue Context >`Request.blueprints` lists the current blueprint followed by its parents. Flask PR #4230 previously fixed this exact callback-order defect. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/flask/app.py[1380-1393] >- src/flask/wrappers.py[180-195] >- src/flask/helpers.py[644-651] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
2. Parent context overrides child 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>Nested template context processors now execute child-first and parent-last, so a parent processor
>overwrites same-named values supplied by the more specific child processor. This reverses the
>established app → parent → child precedence and changes rendered template output.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/flask/app.py[608]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/pull/6216/files#diff-d3e0349504081bb501c611b3954be364188a4cf442056181272e27e830ae446eR608-R608) > >```diff >+ names = chain(names, ctx.request.blueprints) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The blueprint path is returned child-first, while update_template_context applies every processor
>using context.update; consequently, the changed direct traversal lets later parent dictionaries
>replace child values. The historical Flask issue and merged fix identify context processors as one
>of the callback types requiring app-to-child ordering.
>
> > [src/flask/wrappers.py[180-195]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/df5c3e8bd120ea314bedeec8cc6165f3d3b7aafc/src/flask/wrappers.py/#L180-L195) > [src/flask/helpers.py[644-651]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/df5c3e8bd120ea314bedeec8cc6165f3d3b7aafc/src/flask/helpers.py/#L644-L651) > [src/flask/app.py[610-619]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/df5c3e8bd120ea314bedeec8cc6165f3d3b7aafc/src/flask/app.py/#L610-L619) > 🌐 [The issue identifies context processors as affected by the incorrect app → deepest child → parent ordering.](https://github.com/pallets/flask/issues/4229) > 🌐 [The merged Flask change fixed callback ordering for nested blueprints by restoring app-down-to-child traversal.](https://github.com/pallets/flask/pull/4230) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Template context processors for nested blueprints must execute app-first, then parent-to-child, so the closest blueprint has final precedence. Since `request.blueprints` is leaf-first, traversing it directly causes parent processors to overwrite child values. > >## Issue Context >Each processor result is applied with `context.update`, making traversal order observable whenever processors return the same key. Flask PR #4230 previously corrected this exact nested callback ordering. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/flask/app.py[604-619] >- src/flask/wrappers.py[180-195] >- src/flask/helpers.py[644-651] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
3. URL defaults run backwards 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>inject_url_defaults now invokes the closest child blueprint's default functions before its
>parents, reversing the established app → parent → child order. When nested callbacks populate or
>transform the same URL value, the generated URL can use the wrong scope's value.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/flask/sansio/app.py[973]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/pull/6216/files#diff-c57b8f34cffef9948b35aec94cb2364f75c1a2854064a13bf8216603cb1f607bR973-R973) > >```diff >+ names, _split_blueprint_path(endpoint.rpartition(".")[0]) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>_split_blueprint_path emits the fully qualified child first and then its parents, and
>inject_url_defaults passes one shared mutable values dictionary to callbacks in that sequence.
>Nested callback registrations are stored under those qualified names, so removing reversed
>directly changes their observable execution and precedence.
>
> > [src/flask/helpers.py[644-651]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/df5c3e8bd120ea314bedeec8cc6165f3d3b7aafc/src/flask/helpers.py/#L644-L651) > [src/flask/sansio/app.py[967-979]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/df5c3e8bd120ea314bedeec8cc6165f3d3b7aafc/src/flask/sansio/app.py/#L967-L979) > [src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py[379-410]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/df5c3e8bd120ea314bedeec8cc6165f3d3b7aafc/src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py/#L379-L410) > 🌐 [The historical defect explicitly lists `url_defaults` among callbacks incorrectly invoked deepest-blueprint-first.](https://github.com/pallets/flask/issues/4229) > 🌐 [The merged fix corrected nested callback order, including URL-default traversal.](https://github.com/pallets/flask/pull/4230) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >URL-default callbacks for nested blueprint endpoints must run from the application through parent blueprints to the closest child. `_split_blueprint_path` is leaf-first, so its result must be reversed before callback traversal. > >## Issue Context >The callbacks mutate the shared `values` dictionary, making execution order observable for overlapping or dependent values. Flask PR #4230 previously fixed this exact nested URL-default ordering defect. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/flask/sansio/app.py[967-979] >- src/flask/helpers.py[644-651] >- src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py[379-410] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
